title: Transfer work needs evidence the teaching didn't use
statement: Decide whether an item checks taught knowledge, where overlap with the teaching is the point, or independent use of a skill, which needs evidence the teaching never used.
example: One of six repairs behind an AP unit's block was replacing independent tasks in Lessons 1, 3 and 6 that reused answer-bearing evidence from the worked example.
detail: An independent audit of an AP unit confirmed unseen sources and no wrong or ambiguous key, yet blocked it on six repairs, one of them replacing independent tasks in Lessons 1, 3 and 6 that reused answer-bearing modelled evidence; a later commit closed the repairs with an independent, different-evidence release. A Grade 5 course writes the split in as an invariant, keeping independent item claims disjoint from teaching claims while a blocking, unscored on-ramp check retrieves a prior lesson's claim. The reading BrainLift needed five adversarial rounds to isolate the distinction: an in-lesson knowledge check answerable from explicitly taught knowledge is legitimate, the same overlap in a comprehension or transfer item is a leak, and in reading, where finding the answer in the passage is the skill, a history-style 'answer is in the source' check is skipped. Evidence for independent use must also avoid the cases the teaching and its worked example used, so that copying the model can't pass it.
against: In the Grade 5 course the split is a design-level resolution: every lesson's certification still read not run, so whether it works at runtime is unverified. none found; checks of taught knowledge are exempt by design, provided each item's class is stated (`ti-courseplans-audit/skills/train-teacher/references/teacher-contract.md`). The Grade 3 build notes apply disjointness to checks for understanding as well, saying never to test the exact proposition just modeled (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g3-reading/iteration-3/CONTENT-FAILURE-CLASSES.md`, lines 33-34).
